reasoning: A low total (41.5), Iowa's top-10 defense against a Washington offense that can't pass or convert third downs, and Washington's 1-4 ATS mark make a one-score Washington edge at most, so +3 is the side. The most interesting [angle] is Washington losing both Big Ten games by one possession: this projects as a field-goal game. A confirmed Brown absence would have pushed it to a pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before locking (see note), so treat this as graded separately.

BYU's 4-0 ATS run came with LJ Martin; without him (and LB Glasker) the offense produced 216 yards vs TCU, and a slow, run-first game against Iowa State's strong ground attack projects as a one-score BYU win. The line already fell from 14.5 to 9.5, but I still make it about BYU by 6-7. The [angle] that decided it: both teams play slowly, which limits margins. A healthy Martin would have flipped me to a pass.

Pre-game evidence was close: the market sat at -3.5 after touching -4.5, money split toward A&M while tickets were on Missouri, and Missouri was missing two running backs. That made A&M +3.5 a thin lean with Missouri projected by about 2. The most unusual angle was Missouri's lone healthy RB carrying a nation-high workload. A confirmed healthy Missouri backfield, or the line holding at -4.5, would have flipped it to a pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before deciding (see note).

This season's efficiency numbers favored Oklahoma State by a wide margin (OSU's top-15 offense and defense vs a UCF offense outside the top 100 in success rate), and the situation agreed: OSU off a bye, UCF on its sixth straight game, banged up at QB and center. The line also rose from 9.5 to 10.5. UCF's 4-1 ATS record and within-10 streak kept it a lean, not strong. A healthy Barnett or a line move back below 10 would have made it a pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before deciding (see note).

This season's data favored Pitt (4-1 ATS, dominant at home, a strong run game against a UNC defense that bleeds rushing first downs), and UNC's offense ranks 117th in scoring. The Heintschel injury had already been priced in when the line dropped to -3.5, so the lean was Pitt by about 5. The surprising angle was UNC's offense trailing its opponents' rushing first downs alone. A worse report on Geriner's readiness, or sharp money on UNC, would have made it a pass. Contaminated: see note.

This season's defensive numbers decided it: Indiana's top-5 defense against a Nebraska offense whose numbers came from a soft schedule, with the price drifting toward Indiana (-120 / -8.5). Indiana's 1-4 ATS record came from 20+ point spreads and doesn't carry over to -7.5. The surprising angle is the lookahead to Ohio State, which keeps this a lean rather than strong. Sharp money on Nebraska or a Hoover injury would have flipped it to a pass.

The numbers favored Florida, but by about the spread: Dimers projected 12 vs 11.5, and Florida's leaky defense (98th) gives South Carolina's offense a backdoor route. With the projection within a point of the line and Vernell Brown's status undecided, it's a pass. A firm Sellers benching or line movement to -13 would have made it a Florida lean.

A 39.5-point underdog covers only if it can score, and Stanford has been held to single digits in every loss while ranking 131st in scoring. Meanwhile money (86%) pushed the line from 35.5 to 39.5 and Notre Dame has covered every five-TD spot under Freeman. The lookahead to BYU, and Carr possibly resting late, keeps it a lean at about Notre Dame by 45 rather than strong. If the line had reached 42+, or ND had confirmed resting starters early, it would have been a pass.

Two near-identical offenses with Kansas State a bit better on defense, rested and at home, against a Houston defense missing its leading tackler: I make it Kansas State by about 3. That is right on the 2.5 line, so I pass. The best angle is Klein having coached Weigman at A&M, set against Kansas State's thin QB depth. A clear injury to Johnson or a line move off 2.5 would have decided it.

With Moore out, a backup QB making his first Oregon start, a weak Oregon run defense facing the nation's most efficient rushing team, and the market moving down from 11.5-12.5, I had UCLA covering +11.5 (Oregon by about 6.5) before the contamination below. The best angle is the run-game mismatch: it shortens the game, which protects a double-digit dog. A confirmed return by Moore or a move up through 12 would have changed it.

Before contamination the evidence looked balanced: Ole Miss's better offense and the bye against its 1-3 ATS record, a bad defense and Vanderbilt's home streak, with Kalshi pricing the spread close to 50/50. I make it about Ole Miss by 9 against a 9.5 line, so I pass. The best angle was Curtis returning from a knee injury.

This season Texas has played close, low-scoring games against good teams (1-3 ATS, one-score wins over Ohio State and Tennessee), the total is 39.5, and the line fell from 9.5/8 to 7.5 while 72% of tickets were on Texas. I project Texas by about 5, so Oklahoma covers +8.5. The worry is Oklahoma's offense (12.3 ppg over its last three, Mateer's turnovers), which keeps this at a lean. A Mateer benching or the line moving back up to 9+ would have changed it.

Ohio State's form (about +30 a game since Texas, 4-1 ATS) and Maryland's collapse (lost 54-3 to UCLA, a turnover-prone QB) point one way. The sharp move from 35 to 32.5 against 73% public tickets, Ohio State's OL and WR absences, and the Indiana look-ahead point the other. I make it about 32, right on the number, so I pass. A closing number of 30 or lower or 35 or higher would have made it a play.

Tennessee's elite run game against Arkansas's 128th-ranked run defense, and Arkansas losing every P4 game by 27+, point to Tennessee. A first-time starting QB on a team ranked 131st in passing success, close SEC games, an unmoved line and the Alabama look-ahead point to Arkansas. I project about Tennessee by 14, right on 13.5, so I pass. Clarity on Brandon's shoulder (a healthy starter) would have pushed me to Tennessee.

LSU is the better team, but the market went against 60% of the tickets, from 9.5 to 8.5, and the total fell five points. Kentucky has a top-two pass rush, a 34.6-ppg offense and home field against an LSU team missing several starters with an interception-prone QB. I project LSU by about 7, so +9.5 is the side. The [angle] that worried me most is Kentucky's three missing inside linebackers against LSU's offense. Steam toward LSU would have made it a pass.

This season's matchup data point one way: USC's top-10 offense and running game against a Penn State run defense ranked 133rd that just allowed 413 rushing yards, while Penn State's offense ranks near 100th. The market flipped to USC as the favorite on game day, so getting +1.5 is a good number. The [angle] is Penn State's 0-2 Big Ten start under a new staff, without its top receiver. USC's 1-5 ATS mark is the main counterweight, and the reason this is a lean, not strong.

The market moved 4.5 points to Alabama against heavy public Georgia tickets, Alabama's efficiency profile is better (2nd net EPA vs Georgia's 67th on defense), and Georgia is short a running back and a starting defensive lineman. I make Alabama about a 3.5-point favorite, and we hold -1.5 when the market closed -2.5. The [angle] holding this to a lean is the rain and 20+ mph wind forecast, which shrinks margins in a near pick'em.

Utah is clearly better, but Kansas's Big 12-best total defense and a 51-point total make 15.5 a fair number, and the market and models sit within a point of it. Conflicting ATS trends (Utah 1-4 as a top-15 home team, Kansas 1-8 as an October road dog) cancel out. Pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before locking (see note); the pass was my pre-game read.

Boise's efficiency edge (18th vs 79th) points to about a touchdown, but Riley, Jones and Gaines are all hurt, Fresno is 4-1 ATS and 7-3 ATS in the series, and Fresno's lead back is also concussed. I make it Boise by about 5.5, within about 1 point of 6.5, with key players' status deciding it. Pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before locking (see note).

The market decided it. A 1.5-2 point drop from -10 toward Tampa, with the rookie QB start already known and 92% of Circa handle on 33% of tickets, is a strong sharp signal, and the slate's +8.5 sits above Circa's 7.5. Dallas's 31st-ranked defense, which struggles against running QBs, gives a mobile rookie a path to a late score. The most surprising [angle] is Bowles' 4-0 ATS record as a 7.5-14 point road dog. This stays a lean, not strong, because Tampa is 0-13 ATS in its last 13 and has a weak offense. A bad Daniels first half like the one against Green Bay, or Dallas back at -10, would have flipped it.

Philadelphia's offense was already the league's worst by yardage and now loses its RB1, two top WRs, its center and (via retirement/trade) two OL starters, while Jacksonville is healthy and 9-2 ATS as a favorite under Coen. The surprising angle was the Lane Johnson retirement/Jurgens trade gutting the line mid-week. A neutral site, Jax's yardage-allowed number and 72% public on Jax kept it to a lean; a healthy Barkley/Smith would have flipped it to a pass.

Miami can't score with this lineup (11.5 ppg, never more than 13, Willis under constant pressure), which is the key test for a big underdog. Cincinnati gets Chase and Higgins back. The most surprising angle was how lopsided Miami's season numbers are (-55 differential, most rookie starts). Bengals' close-game habit, a dead run game and 75% public tickets held it to a lean; Chase being ruled out would have made it a pass.

The Bears' season numbers (+47, 3-1 ATS, league-best rushing) point one way while a backup QB, an injured RB1 and Love's history vs Chicago point the other; at 1.5 the projection sits on the number. CONTAMINATED: a search summary showed this game's final score before I decided, so this is a pass and should be graded separately.

Cleveland's repeated performance (three straight wins as an underdog, 6-1 ATS in its last seven) plus 10 days of rest against a Jets offense that managed 157 yards last week makes the home favorite hard to back. The rain-and-wind forecast is the angle: in a sub-40 total, 2.5 points matter more. The Jets' move from -1.5 to -2.5 and Mason Graham's absence kept it a lean; clear sharp money on the Jets would have made it a pass.

A winless road team giving 7 in a division game with the lowest total on the board is too much, especially from a Houston side that is 0-4 ATS and allows 27.3 a game while Tennessee has stayed within its number three times. The big move from -3.5 to -7.5 is the strongest counterpoint and is why this is a lean, not strong. A clear injury reason behind the move (none found) would have made it a pass.

The rest and travel gap (Colts back from London with no bye vs Steelers on 10 days) and Indianapolis ranking last in net yards per play point to Pittsburgh at a short number. The London-return angle is the decider; the Colts' 3-1 ATS start and Jonathan Taylor's form are the counterweights. Rodgers or Metcalf missing would have made it a pass.

The Raiders' 4-0 ATS start and 26+ points every week, against a Patriots offense at 16.3 ppg, make +3.5 a live number, especially with New England's top two corners ruled out. The best angle is that both NE starting CBs are out against an 11-TD Cousins. Jeanty's questionable status and the strong move from -8 down to -3.5, which takes some value off LV, keep this a lean. Projection: NE by 1.

Minnesota is 4-0 on an elite defense and +5 turnovers while its offense ranks near the bottom in EPA and success rate. Without Darrisaw, and possibly Jefferson and Addison, it shouldn't be laying points on the road against a Saints offense that scores. The best angle is that Minnesota's top two WRs and LT were all in doubt at once. The Saints' last-ranked defense is the risk; if Jefferson plays fully this is a pass. Projection: NO by 1.

This sits right on the number. Daniels' return justifies Washington -3.5, and the models put it at a coin flip (Stats Insider 50/50; my projection WAS by about 3). The angle is a Giants team at 3-1 on a backup QB against a Washington team getting its franchise QB back from an elbow injury. A healthy McLaurin or a confirmed full-go Daniels would have pushed me to Washington.

Two flawed teams meet. LA's makeshift line and missing receivers justify the 6-point flip, but Denver's offense hasn't shown it can win by margin and its top corner is likely out. My projection of DEN by 3 sits within half a point of the spread, so I pass. The most surprising angle is that the Chargers' starting LT, RT and LG are all out at once. A healthy Surtain would have made it a Denver lean.

Detroit's elite offense against an Arizona defense that has allowed 30+ three straight weeks points to Detroit. Detroit's last-ranked defense, 0-3-1 ATS record and road struggles point back toward Arizona in a projected shootout. My projection of DET by 6 sits right on the 5.5 line, so I pass. The angle is a 3-point market fade of Detroit from the opener despite near-unanimous expert picks on the Lions.

The league's most efficient offense, an unbeaten 49ers team, is getting a full 3 points against a Seattle offense that hasn't improved with Darnold back. That's enough for a lean even without Bosa. The most surprising angle is that the experts and NBC lean Seattle while every efficiency metric favors SF. If the line had dropped to 2.5 I'd pass. Projection: SEA by 0.5.

Before I was contaminated, my number was Atlanta by about 2.5. That is within a point of the -3 line, so I was headed for a pass. The [angle] that Atlanta's league-best run defense meets Henry and a backup QB points to Atlanta, while the overcorrected line, Baltimore's road-dog ATS history and Atlanta's 1-4 ATS record as a home favorite since 2025 point to Baltimore. The spread money was split 50/50. I'm locking a pass, the call I would have made without the leak.

What decided it: sharp money moved the line from -2.5/-3 to -3.5 (87% of Circa handle on 36% of tickets), and the efficiency gap on defense is large (Rams 3rd in opponent EPA, Bills 30th, now without Ed Oliver). Getting the Rams at -2.5 is a better number than the market's close. The most surprising [angle] cuts the other way: Stafford is poor against zone and Buffalo plays zone 78% of the time. This is a lean, not strong, because Buffalo's 31.8-PPG offense and a 54.5 total leave backdoor risk. A DJ Moore return and a line back to -2.5 with sharp money on Buffalo would have changed it.
